text:
Boston arrives with points in eight straight (7-0-1) and a 6-4 win over San Jose on Saturday, a game the Bruins trailed in the third period. Casey Mittelstadt reached 100 career goals in it, and Mark Kastelic plays his 300th NHL game tonight. Carolina, 3-1-1 in its last five, shut out St. Louis 4-0, with Pyotr Kochetkov stopping all 24 shots. The Hurricanes are without Mark Jankowski and Jordan Staal, and Nicolas Deslauriers and Felix Unger Sörum are taking on bigger minutes in their place.

Our numbers favor Carolina, 3.32 expected goals to 2.72. The Hurricanes create better chances (3.89 expected goals per 60 minutes against Boston's 3.28) and give up fewer (2.49 against 3.06). Boston's results are ahead of its play: a +22 goal difference, powered by finishing and goaltending. The Bruins also take 4.7 penalties a game, which matters against a Carolina power play averaging 0.92 expected goals a game. In net, projected starters Jeremy Swayman (+6.1 goals saved above expected, a measure of how many goals a goalie has prevented beyond what the shot quality suggested) and Kochetkov (+4.6) have both been sharp this season. Swayman has the far longer track record, at +26.5 last year to Kochetkov's -0.03.

Watch David Pastrnak, who has a 70% chance at a point, and Sebastian Aho, at 71% for Carolina. Logan Stankoven has scored in three straight and sits one goal from 50 career goals.
